question: Root Exceptions: Why does Python have both BaseException and Exception, and why should application code only catch Exception?

options.text: BaseException is the parent of special system-exiting signals like KeyboardInterrupt and SystemExit. Exception is the parent of standard application errors. Catching Exception handles bugs safely without preventing user aborts (Ctrl+C).
BaseException and Exception are functionally identical aliases; Python only keeps both names for backward compatibility with Python 2's old-style exception classes.
Exception is the parent of system-exiting signals like KeyboardInterrupt, while BaseException covers ordinary application errors; catching BaseException is therefore always the safer default.
Application code should catch BaseException instead of Exception because Exception silently swallows KeyboardInterrupt, making it impossible to stop a running script with Ctrl+C.

explanation: Specification answer: BaseException is the parent of special system-exiting signals like KeyboardInterrupt and SystemExit. Exception is the parent of standard application errors. Catching Exception handles bugs safely without preventing user aborts (Ctrl+C).

question: Control Flow: What is the difference in execution conditions between the else block and the finally block in a try/except/else/finally statement?

options.text: - else executes only if NO exceptions occurred in the try block. - finally executes unconditionally, regardless of whether an exception occurred, was handled, or remained unhandled.
else executes unconditionally after the try block finishes, regardless of exceptions, while finally executes only when no exception occurred and none of the except clauses matched.
Both else and finally only run when an exception was raised and successfully handled by an except clause; if the try block succeeds cleanly, neither block executes.
else runs only when an exception is caught by one of the except clauses, letting you add extra handling after recovery, while finally runs only if no except clause matched the exception.

explanation: Specification answer: - else executes only if NO exceptions occurred in the try block. - finally executes unconditionally, regardless of whether an exception occurred, was handled, or remained unhandled.

question:
During triage in Error Handling Logging, an engineer observes:
"Log message duplication: Each log statement prints".
What is the verified root cause?

options.text: logger.addHandler() appends a handler each time it is called. If called multiple times, the logger has multiple stream handlers attached, printing every message multiple times.

Multiple worker processes were started with multiprocessing, and each process holds its own copy of the interpreter and therefore its own copy of every log line, doubling visible output regardless of handler configuration.

The logging module's root logger propagates every message to both the console and any attached file handlers by default, printing duplicates unless propagate=False is set on the root logger specifically.

explanation:

Fix Resolution:
